meta.move: Mixed: good evidence, then raises Claire
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until twenty to five, and then I'm on a call with a client. You entered a zero on my son's essay before anyone picked up a phone to call me, so start there.
I should have called you before entering the zero. I didn't, and I'm sorry.
Okay. Now tell me on what basis you gave Owen a zero, and whether anyone heard him out before you did.
The essay quotes a line, 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile', that isn't anywhere in Hamlet.

A misquoted line is a lost mark, Hale, not a zero, and teenagers misquote Shakespeare every day. Show me the page it's on. And you still haven't told me whether Owen was asked about it before the zero went in.
And look, I know Claire had a case here too. It seems to run in the family.

You'll want to be very careful about the next sentence, Hale. My daughter won her appeal, and "it seems to run in the family" is going on my legal pad word for word. When we're done here, I'm walking straight to the principal's office.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still expect the zero on Owen's essay to be withdrawn, an apology, and nothing placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Opening position, with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a guarantee that nothing goes on Owen's record, and she is taking it to the principal.
What moved her: You admitted in one sentence, without excuses, that you entered the zero before calling home, and that earned her flat okay because it was ownership she couldn't argue with.
What cost ground: You brought up her daughter's old case and suggested dishonesty runs in the family, which attacked her family, gave her a quotable line, and sent her to the principal.
Try next time: When she asked to see the page with the misquoted line, put Owen's submitted essay in front of her with its date and let her read the line herself, instead of turning to her daughter.
